videos.script: Every class so far has had a file to itself. This lesson puts classes inside other classes, and there are four ways to do it. {{static}} The first is a static nested class. It lives inside another class for the sake of its name and its access, and nothing more. You can make one without ever making the outer object. {{inner}} Drop the word static and it becomes an inner class. Now every object of it belongs to one object of the outer class. A library card belongs to a member, and borrowing on the card counts against that member. {{hidden}} Then a look inside the class file, where the compiler keeps that owner in a field nobody wrote. {{anonymous}} Last, two classes declared inside a method. One has a name only the method can use. The other has no name at all, and it is how Java passed behaviour around before lambdas. {{capture}} Both can read the method's local variables, with one condition the compiler enforces. By the end you can tell the four kinds apart, and you know which one to reach for first.
